import pyodbc
import pandas as pd

conn = pyodbc.connect(
  "DRIVER={ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server};"
  "SERVER=localhost;"
  "DATABASE=AdventureWorks2012;"
  "Trusted_Connection=yes;"
)
caption: pyodbc — Python's standard way to talk to SQL Server.

eyebrow: A real query, straight into a DataFrame
code:
query = """
SELECT TOP 10 ProductID, Name, ListPrice
FROM Production.Product
WHERE ListPrice > 0
ORDER BY ListPrice DESC;
"""

df = pd.read_sql(query, conn)
conn.close()
caption: Real T-SQL, against the same AdventureWorks2012 from this site's T-SQL course — back as a DataFrame directly.

eyebrow: Always close the connection — Lesson 19's finally
code:
conn = pyodbc.connect(...)
try:
    df = pd.read_sql(query, conn)
finally:
    conn.close()
caption: Closes whether the query succeeded or failed — never leaks an open connection.
